analysis: Documentation-only change in docs/developer/test.md: bumps the 'Last updated' stamp (line 3) and adds an 'Add-On Hold' test section (head ~767-790, per the changed-range map). The head unit shown ends at line 474 and the base unit starts at 946, so the added section's text is not visible in the supplied excerpts and I could only read it from the truncated patch. No code, config, protocol, key, attestation, cache or authorization behavior is modified. The patch text indicates the new tests bind a real AF_UNIX socket and take a flock in a private temporary runtime directory, need no credentials or model weights, and exercise hold.v1 IPC, peer policy, drain ownership and heartbeat/register wire encodings. No threat-model asset or trust boundary (TB-002, TB-003, TB-011, T-041 and others) is weakened. The doc says tests run without credentials or live provider state and use private temp dirs, which is consistent with the isolation guidance elsewhere in the file. Remaining integration question: the add-on hold feature itself (local IPC socket, peer policy, draining heartbeat, 503 rejection) is new attack surface that presumably ships in other files of this PR. The threat model does not appear to cover it, so those source files need review for local-peer authentication (TB-003 operator vs process) and for the hold's effect on the availability and serving-authorization boundary. This unit's visible evidence cannot confirm that, so a deeper review of the non-doc files is warranted.
